speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin my evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning. Given your history of anabolic steroid use, heavy smoking, and significant weight loss alongside progressive arm weakness, could you tell me if the weakness is specifically in the biceps and triceps, or if it involves your hand and fingers as well?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive weakness, sensory loss, and a "dull aching and burning" pain pattern in your right arm is very suggestive of a nerve compression or infiltration issue, especially given your history of heavy smoking and steroid use. Have you noticed any visible wasting (shrinking) of the muscles in your right arm, or any specific numbness in a ring-like distribution around your hand?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of heavy smoking, steroid use, and the progressive nature of your right arm weakness and sensory loss, I need to visualize the extent of the pathology. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI of the right shoulder and arm. Also, can you confirm if the weakness is limited strictly to the right arm or if you have any weakness in your legs or difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning a shirt? REQUEST TEST: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Right Shoulder/Arm: Not performed. CT Chest: Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor. Serum Creatine Kinase (CK): Not performed. Neurological Exam: 2/5 strength in right arm, 5/5 strength in left arm; Decreased sensation in right arm; Normal reflexes; Unaffected coordination. Vital Signs: BP 177/108 mmHg, Temp 99.5°F, HR 90/min, RR 17/min, O2 Sat 98%.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan reveals a solid mass at the apex of your right lung, which likely explains your progressive arm weakness, sensory loss, and pain due to compression of the brachial plexus. Given your history of heavy smoking, this is highly concerning for a Pancoast tumor. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Brachial Plexopathy.
